evals.name: build-from-scratch-pharmacy
evals.prompt: Estou começando um sistema de gestão pra uma rede de farmácias (Laravel + Postgres). Preciso implementar emissão de NF-e (venda de produtos) e NFS-e (quando cobramos por aplicação de injetáveis, por exemplo) usando a Focus NFe. Nunca mexi com nota fiscal eletrônica antes. Como eu estruturo esse módulo do zero? Pode me dar um plano de arquitetura e os pontos de atenção mais importantes antes de eu começar a codar.
evals.expected_output: A layered architecture (provider abstraction separate from tax-rule resolution), an explicit 'never guess a fiscal value' principle with concrete examples (block-and-ask pattern), correct CFOP/CST-CSOSN distinction for NF-e vs correct ISS-por-dentro handling for NFS-e, awareness that Focus NFe responses need polling despite looking synchronous, and homologação vs produção guidance.

assertions.text: Recommends separating provider/vendor-adapter code from tax-rule resolution logic (an architecture boundary), not just 'call the Focus API'
States explicitly that fiscal values must never be guessed/defaulted when missing — should block/ask instead
Distinguishes that NF-e (goods) uses CFOP/ICMS rules while NFS-e (services) uses ISS rules — not treated as the same computation
Explains ISS is computed 'por dentro' (embedded in the price), not added on top of the subtotal
Notes that Focus NFe responses need to be polled/checked for final status, not treated as synchronous just because the initial call returns fast
Distinguishes homologação vs. produção as separate environments with separate data, not just separate API keys

evals.name: extend-existing-discount-nodejs
evals.prompt: Tenho um e-commerce em Node/Express já integrado com a Focus NFe pra emitir NF-e das vendas. Agora quero adicionar um desconto por cupom antes de emitir a nota. Não sei se isso mexe só no valor total ou se afeta outras coisas do documento fiscal. Como eu implemento isso com segurança?
evals.expected_output: Should flag that discount changes the tax base (not just a display total), warn about rounding/float precision, and not conflate a discount change with a CFOP change.

assertions.text: Explicitly says the discount changes the tax base used for the fiscal document, not just a cosmetic display total
Warns about rounding/floating-point precision when subtracting the discount before it feeds into fiscal calculations
Does not just say 'subtract X% from the total' without any caveat about where in the pipeline that has to happen
Mentions validating/blocking on missing or inconsistent data rather than assuming a safe default when applying the discount
Shows awareness that CFOP itself is about operation type (not value), so reassures or clarifies whether CFOP needs re-resolution — doesn't conflate discount with a CFOP change

evals.name: debug-stuck-processando-spedy
evals.prompt: Um cliente meu relatou que uma nota fiscal (NFC-e) emitida via Spedy ficou travada em status 'processando' há 3 dias e nada aconteceu — o cliente já pagou e o produto já saiu, mas a nota nunca autorizou nem rejeitou. Como eu investigo isso?
evals.expected_output: A structured triage distinguishing polling failure from real vendor status, checking the raw vendor response, and not jumping straight to cancel/reissue.

assertions.text: First step is getting the exact document reference / integrationId, not guessing from a vague description
Explicitly distinguishes 'we never got a real answer back from Spedy' (transient/retryable) from 'Spedy genuinely returned processando' as different situations
Recommends checking the actual/raw response from Spedy's status-check call, not just trusting the status stored in the local database
Does not jump straight to 'just cancel and reissue' before diagnosing root cause
Mentions the Spedy-specific quirk that there's no GET-by-reference — you poll a list endpoint filtered by your own integrationId
